notes: Re-read arXiv version 1, dated 10 July 2026, on 23 September 2026. Corrected the earlier registry title and normalized the arXiv URL. Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 give necessary residue-rate conditions for a code realized by one fixed positive odd integer: the binary start representative eventually equals that integer, and the ternary endpoint representative eventually equals the actual endpoint. The paper does not prove a fixed-root inverse-count lower bound or termination; its finite evolutionary search is explicitly diagnostic. The existing comparison is docs/literature_comparison.md: its affine numerator B_m is the laboratory's word offset C, and its r is the start residue R modulo 2^K. Applicability audit: docs/problems/collatz_conditioned_syracuse.md.
title: Adaptive Search in Collatz Exponent-Code Space via 2-adic and 3-adic Constraints
